senses.definition: to renounce or reject something desired or valuable
senses.example: The monk abnegated all worldly pleasures.

senses.definition: the protection, backing or support of a particular person or organization
senses.example: The festival is held under the aegis of the city council.

senses.definition: self-confidence or assurance, especially when in a demanding situation
senses.example: She handled the hostile questions with aplomb.

senses.definition: to take or claim something for oneself without justification
senses.example: The committee arrogated to itself the power to hire staff.

senses.definition: respected and impressive
senses.example: The prize was awarded by an august panel of scholars.

senses.definition: a secret political clique or faction
senses.example: A cabal of generals planned the coup.

senses.definition: the making of false and defamatory statements in order to damage someone's reputation
senses.example: She was the victim of a campaign of calumny.

senses.definition: to support the cause of; to defend
senses.example: She championed the rights of tenants for decades.

senses.definition: a person who fights or argues for a cause or on behalf of someone else
senses.example: He was a champion of free speech.

senses.definition: to stop or slow down the progress of something undesirable
senses.example: Firebreaks helped check the spread of the blaze.

senses.definition: a stop or restraint on the progress of something
senses.example: The courts act as a check on executive power.

senses.definition: courteous and considerate behavior toward others
senses.example: The comity between the two neighbors survived the dispute over the fence.

senses.definition: an association of nations for their mutual benefit
senses.example: Free trade was seen as the basis of a comity of nations.

senses.definition: naturally accompanying or associated
senses.example: The job brought fame and its concomitant loss of privacy.

senses.definition: a phenomenon that naturally accompanies or follows something
senses.example: Stress is often a concomitant of rapid change.

senses.definition: a person or thing that is the center of attention or admiration
senses.example: The new art museum is the cynosure of the waterfront.

senses.definition: to kill, destroy or remove a large proportion of
senses.example: The disease decimated the elm trees of the region.

words.note: Decimate originally meant to kill one in every ten; it now means to destroy a large part of something.

senses.definition: of or having indigestion or consequent irritability or depression
senses.example: The dyspeptic critic hated every play of the season.

senses.definition: to erase a mark from a surface
senses.example: Time had effaced the inscription on the stone.

senses.definition: to make oneself appear insignificant or inconspicuous
senses.example: She effaced herself at parties, staying in the kitchen.

senses.definition: affected, overrefined and ineffectual
senses.example: The novel satirizes the effete aristocrats of the court.

senses.definition: a speech or piece of writing that praises someone or something highly
senses.example: The obituary was a long encomium to the late senator.

senses.definition: extremely bad or unpleasant
senses.example: The food at the motel was execrable.

senses.definition: silly and pointless
senses.example: He made a fatuous remark about the weather during the funeral.

senses.definition: to keep a thought or feeling, typically a negative one, in one's mind, especially secretly
senses.example: He harbored a grudge against his old teacher.

senses.definition: to shelter or hide a criminal or wanted person
senses.example: It is a crime to harbor a fugitive.

senses.definition: to talk to someone in a bullying way
senses.example: The sergeant hectored the new recruits.

senses.definition: leadership or dominance, especially by one country or social group over others
senses.example: The empire's hegemony lasted for centuries.

senses.definition: to enclose or confine someone against their will
senses.example: The prisoner was immured in a tower for years.

senses.definition: having a particular habit, activity or interest that is long-established and unlikely to change
senses.example: He is an inveterate liar.

senses.definition: a huge, powerful and overwhelming force or institution
senses.example: The retail juggernaut drove many small shops out of business.

senses.definition: tearful or given to weeping
senses.example: The lachrymose film had the whole audience reaching for tissues.

senses.definition: promiscuous and unprincipled in sexual matters
senses.example: The novel was banned for its licentious content.

senses.definition: many and various
senses.example: The benefits of the plan are manifold.

senses.definition: (of a thing) in terminal decline; lacking vitality or vigor
senses.example: The town's moribund shipyards finally closed.

senses.definition: in the form of a cloud or haze; hazy
senses.example: A nebulous glow surrounded the street lamps in the fog.

senses.definition: (of a concept) unclear, vague or ill-defined
senses.example: The plan's goals were nebulous.

senses.definition: having an extremely offensive smell
senses.example: A noisome odor rose from the drains.

senses.definition: disagreeable; unpleasant
senses.example: His noisome habits made him a poor roommate.

words.note: Noisome has nothing to do with noise.

senses.definition: to cease developing; to become stagnant or rigid
senses.example: Without new members, the club's traditions ossified.

senses.definition: to turn into bone or bony tissue
senses.example: The cartilage ossifies as the child grows.

senses.definition: a public speech or published text in praise of someone or something
senses.example: The biography reads like a panegyric.

senses.definition: unwilling to spend money or use resources; stingy or frugal
senses.example: The parsimonious old man reused tea bags three times.

senses.definition: belonging to or characteristic of the aristocracy
senses.example: Her patrician accent marked her as wealthy.

senses.definition: an aristocrat or nobleman
senses.example: The patricians of Rome held most of the land.

senses.definition: holding firmly to an opinion or a course of action
senses.example: The pertinacious reporter called every day for a month.

senses.definition: a feeling of irritation or resentment resulting from a slight, especially to one's pride
senses.example: She left the room in a fit of pique.

senses.definition: to stimulate interest or curiosity
senses.example: The mysterious letter piqued her curiosity.

senses.definition: of or occurring every day; daily
senses.example: The novel finds beauty in quotidian routines.

senses.definition: (of a person) formidable, especially as an opponent
senses.example: She was a redoubtable debater.

senses.definition: composure or coolness, sometimes excessive, as shown in danger or under trying circumstances
senses.example: She landed the plane with remarkable sangfroid.

senses.definition: (of a person or their manner) slow and gloomy
senses.example: The saturnine detective rarely smiled.

senses.definition: given to moralizing in a pompous or affected manner
senses.example: The novel is weighed down by sententious asides.

senses.definition: having many curves and turns
senses.example: A sinuous river wound through the valley.

senses.definition: lithe and supple
senses.example: The dancer moved with sinuous grace.

senses.definition: to cause to lose enthusiasm and initiative, especially as a result of a tedious or restrictive routine
senses.example: The rigid rules stultified the young teachers.

senses.definition: deceit used in order to achieve one's goal
senses.example: They gained entry to the building by subterfuge.

senses.definition: bad-tempered and unfriendly
senses.example: The surly waiter slammed down our plates.

senses.definition: to postpone consideration of a motion or bill
senses.example: The committee tabled the proposal until next year.

words.note: In American usage, to table a proposal is to set it aside; in British usage, it is to present it for discussion.

senses.definition: excessive confidence or boldness; audacity
senses.example: He had the temerity to call the queen by her first name.

senses.definition: exhibiting different colors, especially as irregular patches or streaks
senses.example: The plant has variegated leaves of cream and green.

senses.definition: marked by variety
senses.example: She had a long and variegated career.

senses.definition: speaking or representing the truth
senses.example: The jury trusted the veracious witness.
